title: Altitude Formula in Terms of Base and Base Angles
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: In triangle ABC, let b be the length of base AC, let \alpha and \gamma be the interior angles at vertices A and C respectively, and let h be the length of the perpendicular altitude drawn from vertex B to side b. Prove that h = \frac{b\tan\alpha\tan\gamma}{\tan\alpha + \tan\gamma}.

steps.title: Partition Base b Using the Foot of the Altitude
steps.explanation: Let D be the foot of the perpendicular from B to side AC, splitting the base of length b into segments AD = x_1 and DC = x_2.
steps.why: The altitude divides triangle ABC into two right triangles ABD and CBD sharing leg BD = h.

steps.title: Express Segments x_1 and x_2 Using Tangent Ratios
steps.explanation: In right triangle ABD, tan(alpha) = h/x_1; in right triangle CBD, tan(gamma) = h/x_2. Solve each relation for the horizontal segment length.
steps.why: In any right triangle, the adjacent leg equals the opposite leg divided by the tangent of the angle.

steps.title: Sum the Segments and Solve for h
steps.explanation: Substitute x_1 and x_2 into b = x_1 + x_2, factor out h, combine the fractions over the common denominator tan(alpha)*tan(gamma), and solve for h.
steps.why: Multiplying both sides by (tan alpha tan gamma)/(tan alpha + tan gamma) isolates h.
